messages:
anna-support: Hey team — customer ACME reports a big drop in embeddings throughput after last night's rollout. Tokens/sec looks normal but vectors/sec is ~50% of baseline. They've sent sample payloads and timing traces. Can someone triage?

mike-ml: Which model/variant and region? Any recent batching/quantization rollouts?

anna-support: Model: open-embed-1.2 (quantized variant q4_0), region: us-west-2. Rollout: autoscale + new batching-window heuristics pushed at 02:15 UTC. Sample cURL from customer:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1.2-q4_0","input":["..." , "..."]}'
```

ella: (note: renamed here to eli-engineer) Gotcha. Do we see any dimension mismatch errors in runtime logs? Those usually cause fallback to slower code paths.

eli-engineer: Quick check of serving logs around the rollout shows many kernel-selection fallbacks:

```
[2026-03-17T02:16:03Z] kernel_selector: selected kernel 'attn_opt_v2' for seq_len=128
[2026-03-17T02:16:04Z] kernel_selector: fallback to 'attn_generic' for model=open-embed-1.2-q4_0 reason=batch_dim_misaligned
[2026-03-17T02:16:04Z] runtime: using 'compat_exec' path, opt_level=low
```

eli-engineer: That `batch_dim_misaligned` is suspicious — suggests the batching window now groups different-dim payloads or an upstream converter changed pad behavior.

sre-jay: Metrics: GPU utilization spiked to 98% but avg batch size dropped. Queue depth (requests waiting in batcher) rose from ~12 to ~120 during the drop. Prom query I ran: 

```
max_over_time(increase(batcher_queue_depth[5m])[30m:5m])
```

sre-jay: Also saw a surge in small batches (<4) which increases per-token overhead.

mike-ml: Two hypotheses: 1) batching heuristics now allow mixing vectors with slightly different inferred dims triggering compat path; 2) a kernel or autotuner change made the optimal kernel selection less likely for q4 quantized weights, falling back to a slower generic kernel. Either case would raise GPU utilization while lowering vectors/sec.

anna-support: Customer also noted intermittent 400s when they sent batched requests with variable-length items — could be related. Error snippet they saw: `invalid_input_dim: expected 768 got 770`

eli-engineer: That error nails it — dimension mismatch. The batcher should split by embedding dim before batching. Repro steps I recommend to validate locally:

1) run the following Python loop to send mixed-dim payloads to a test endpoint (staging):

```
import requests
url = 'https://staging.redwood/v1/embeddings'
for i in range(100):
    inputs = ["x"] * (2 if i%2==0 else 3)  # alternate small vs medium
    r = requests.post(url, json={"model":"open-embed-1.2-q4_0","input": inputs}, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer ...'})
    print(r.status_code, r.elapsed.total_seconds())
```

2) tail the runtime logs and grep for `batch_dim_misaligned` and kernel_selector fallbacks.

mike-ml: If repro confirms, quick mitigation: 1) force batcher to split by declared dim (config flag), 2) temporarily pin kernel selection to pre-rollout commit (rollback autotuner) for q4_0 variants.

sre-jay: I can enforce a batcher policy change for the impacted fleet (us-west-2) to split on explicit dimension within the next 10 minutes. Will also throttle batch window to 20ms.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout "batcher-dim-split-protect" started at 2026-03-17T02:30:05Z by sre-jay :rocket:

anna-support: Awesome — I've told the customer we have a mitigation in flight and asked for any repro payloads. Please keep me posted and I'll update the ticket.

eli-engineer: Action items: eli -> add unit test for variable-dim batching; mike -> check autotuner commit diff for q4 kernel heuristics; sre-jay -> deploy and monitor vectors/sec / gpu_queue_depth for 30m.

mike-ml: One more note — also check tokenization path: if tokenization output shape changed (padding vs truncation), it can silently alter inferred dims.

anna-support: Thanks all. Marking this as customer P1 escalation.
